title: Formal coefficient strata and one-step blowup formulas
statement:
Let $X\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed finite-type scheme in a smooth scheme over a characteristic-zero field. Fix a point $a$ and its Taylor ideal $K\subset L[[W,Z]]$, where $L=\kappa(a)$. Suppose there are regular coefficient models and generators $f_i=\sum_\gamma c_{i\gamma}(W)Z^\gamma$ with orders $d_i$ satisfying all five division and Jacobian conditions explicitly stated in [lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data]. Write $H_K(n)=\dim_L L[[W,Z]]/(K+(W,Z)^{n+1})$, the extended function computed by the Taylor module. The local equality locus for the extended Hilbert--Samuel function through $a$ is cut out, as a set, by $Z=0$ and the inequalities $\operatorname{ord}c_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$; this assertion also applies to the regular coefficient models of that node.
Let $C$ be a smooth coordinate center contained in this germ, let $\sigma$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], and transform the ideal $K$ by saturation of its total transform by the exceptional equation, so as to define scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform]. At a point $a'$ of the exceptional fibre, $H_{K',a'}\le H_K$. Equality holds if and only if $a'$ belongs to the strict transform of $Z=0$ and, in its nonempty charts with exceptional coordinate $e$,
$$\operatorname{ord}_{a'}c'_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|,\qquad c'_{i\gamma}=e^{-(d_i-|\gamma|)}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}.$$
The quotients in this formula are regular. At equality points the transformed $f_i$ satisfy the same five conditions with the same vertex diagram, and have coefficients $c'_{i\gamma}$. For the blowup of an intersection of two boundary coordinate hyperplanes transverse to $Z=0$, use total transform of $K$ and ordinary pullback $c'_{i\gamma}=\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$; the same five conditions persist and the Hilbert--Samuel function is unchanged at corresponding closed points. Adjoining an independent formal variable takes ordinary pullbacks of the coefficients and sums the Hilbert--Samuel function once. These formulas hold over residue-field extensions and for regular coefficient models after etale localization.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; detailed local input: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207--302, Theorem 7.14, Theorems 7.20--7.21, and the proof of Theorem 9.4; Bierstone--Milman--Temkin, arXiv:0905.3580, section 6.2. No Stacks tag states this formal transform criterion.

proof.text: Write $X=(W,Z)$ and use the blocks, supports and $Q$ of the hypothesis [lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data]. Conditions (1)--(3) and [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] give $H_K=H_D$ by zero remainders. They also show that the homogeneous initial ideal $J=\operatorname{in}K$ is generated by $H_i=\operatorname{in}f_i$: in a supported expansion of $f\in K$, its least homogeneous part is the sum of the least-degree $q_iH_i$, with no cancellation by homogeneous uniqueness. Conversely $H_i\in J$. The $H_i$ retain (1),(2),(4),(5): take the appropriate least homogeneous parts of the identities in (4),(5). They also retain (3) for the ideal $J A$: every homogeneous component of $\sum_ia_iH_i$ is $\sum_i(a_i)_{t-d_i}H_i$, so $\operatorname{in}(JA)=J=\operatorname{in}K$. A quotient by an ideal and by its initial ideal have the same jet dimensions, so $H_{JA}=H_K=H_D$, and the Hilbert criterion of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division], applied to the family $H_i$, gives zero remainders on $JA$, i.e. supported expansions. The $Z$-Jacobian in (4) is the same constant invertible matrix. The empty family has $K=0$, $Z=\varnothing$, $H_K(n)=\binom{n+\dim M}{\dim M}$; all subsequent operations then have the asserted formulas directly. A blowup along the whole ambient germ has no exceptional points. We henceforth treat a nonempty coordinate center ideal.

source.place: BM 7.3--7.6 and (7.2); ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the route.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-formal-hilbert-stratum-minors] to the five conditions. Its cumulative minors ideal is $E=(\partial^\nu f_i:|\nu|<d_i)$. The derivatives $g_j$ in (4) belong to $E$ and to $(Z)$, and writing $g=A(W,Z)Z$, the invertible constant Jacobian is $A(0)$; the formal inverse of $A$ gives $(g_j)=(Z)$. Modulo $(Z)$, the derivatives generating $E$ become $\gamma!\,\partial_W^\beta c_{i\gamma}$ with $|\beta|+|\gamma|<d_i$; all factorials are units. Thus
$$E=(Z,\partial_W^\beta c_{i\gamma}:|\beta|<d_i-|\gamma|).$$
The minors theorem identifies its zero-set germ with the Hilbert equality germ. Its local finite-values hypothesis is supplied by [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control], applied on $X$: the Taylor ideal is that of the closed subscheme and the points compared lie in $X$. At each point $b$, use the centered Taylor map $\tau_b$ of [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus]: it factors through the completion at the $\kappa(b)$-rational point of $M_{\kappa(b)}$. Its faithful flatness contracts equality of extended finite ideals to equality in $\mathcal O_{M,b}$; coherence then extends that equality to a neighbourhood. This is the ambient-dimensional Taylor ring even when $b$ is nonclosed. Vanishing of the displayed derivatives at $x\in N$ is exactly the coefficient order inequalities. This proves the first assertion, including regular coefficient models; it does not translate an arbitrary infinite formal series to another point.

For a permissible center write $W=(T,Y)$ and $I_C=(Y,Z)=P$, so $C\subset N=V(Z)$. Put $b_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|>0$. Along $C$, every coefficient has order at least $b_{i\gamma}$. Each derivative in the $Y$ directions of degree below $b_{i\gamma}$ therefore restricts to zero on the reduced smooth $C$. Expanding in these normal coordinates gives $\tau_b^N(c_{i\gamma})\in(Y)^{b_{i\gamma}}$ in the Taylor ring on $N$ at each $b\in C$. Use the Taylor map on $N$ defined in [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus], through completion at the rational point of $N_{\kappa(b)}$. Faithful flatness contracts this to membership in $I_{C\subset N,b}^{b_{i\gamma}}$: compare that ideal with its sum with $(c_{i\gamma})$. This includes nonclosed $b$. Consequently $f_i\in P^{d_i}$; its ordinary order $d_i$ gives equality $\operatorname{ord}_P f_i=d_i$. Apply [lem-trf-coordinate-blowup-division-generators] to conclude that the saturated strict transform is generated by the regular formal series $f_i'=e^{-d_i}\sigma^*f_i$. This uses scheme-theoretic saturation, not a replacement by a fixed uniform controlled transform of $K$.

source.place: BM 7.19, Lemma 7.22, Corollary 7.24, proof of Theorem 9.4.

proof.text: Here is the finite-jet rank calculation used below. For finitely many series $h_i(\lambda,X)$ whose coefficients are polynomial in $\lambda$, truncate all $X^\beta h_i$ modulo $(X)^{n+1}$ to get a finite polynomial matrix $A_n(\lambda)$. If its cokernel dimension is the same $h(n)$ for all nonzero $\lambda\in L$, every minor larger than that common rank vanishes at infinitely many scalars and hence is the zero polynomial. Thus the cokernel dimension at $\lambda=0$ is at least $h(n)$. In particular: replacing $h_i(U,V)$ by $h_i(0,V)$ cannot decrease $H$, by using $h_i(\lambda U,V)$; substituting $U_2=U_1(c+U_2)$ cannot decrease $H$, by using $U_2=\lambda U_2+(1-\lambda)U_1(c+U_2)$; and for homogeneous $H_i$ the ideal $J_v=(H_i(X+v))$ has $H_{J_v}\le H_J$, by using $H_i(X+\lambda v)$ and scalar dilation when $\lambda\ne0$. Each assertion holds at every jet order, since the indicated substitutions for nonzero $\lambda$ are invertible (up to multiplying homogeneous generators by units). Characteristic zero ensures $L$ is infinite.

source.place: BM Lemmas 7.25--7.26 and the scaling argument preceding (7.27); agent-written finite-matrix argument.

proof.text: We also record the elementary homogeneous restriction test used for each prefix. If its vertices have zero $U$ components, its quotient supports are $\mathbf N^{|U|}\times\Delta_i^V$. Unique homogeneous division for $H_i(U,V)$ is equivalent to division for $H_i(0,V)$. Indeed in each fixed total degree order rows and columns by increasing $U$ degree. The division matrix is block triangular, with diagonal blocks copies of the division matrices for $H_i(0,V)$. It is invertible exactly when those diagonal blocks are invertible. This also proves that $H_i(0,V)\ne0$ for every vertex. In particular, a homogeneous family with the same pure-essential restrictions as a given prefix inherits its homogeneous division; the number of indexed columns equals the number of monomials, so spanning and uniqueness coincide.

source.place: BM Lemma 7.7 and Remark 7.8, printed pp.263--264; block triangular finite-dimensional calculation.

proof.text: We need a strict comparison for translated homogeneous ideals. Apply [lem-trf-formal-hilbert-stratum-minors] to the $H_i$ and $J$. Its minors and derivative ideals are homogeneous polynomial ideals: a matrix entry has weight $d_i+|\beta|-|\alpha|$, so each minor is homogeneous. Equality after completion at zero implies equality degree by degree of these polynomial ideals. At a translation $v=(0,\zeta)$ with $\zeta\ne0$, one of the linear forms $\partial^{\beta_j}H_{i(j)}$ is nonzero: these are the components of the invertible constant matrix in (4) applied to $\zeta$. Thus some rank-increasing minor is nonzero at $v$. At its jet order the translated ideal has strictly smaller cokernel than $J$. Step 4 gives $H_{J_v}\le H_J$ in every degree, so $H_{J_{(0,\zeta)}}<H_J$ in lexicographic order. This is the strict assertion (7.27), derived from the cited minors statement rather than assumed as another transform theorem.

Let the projective direction above $a$ be $[\eta:\zeta]$ in the $(Y,Z)$ directions. First suppose $\eta_1=1$ after relabelling. In completed chart coordinates write
$$T=S,\quad Y_1=e,\quad Y_j=e(\eta_j+U_j)\ (j>1),\quad Z=e(\zeta+V).$$
If $h_{i\gamma}$ is the degree-$(d_i-|\gamma|)$ part of $c_{i\gamma}$, the center-order computation shows that it depends only on $Y$, and
$$f_i'|_{S=e=0}=\sum_{|\gamma|\le d_i}h_{i\gamma}(1,\widetilde\eta+U)(\zeta+V)^\gamma=H_i'.$$
Consequently step 4 gives $H_{K'}\le H_{(H_i')}$. The invertible substitution $T=S$, $Y_1=e$, $Y_j=(1+e)(\eta_j+U_j)-\eta_j$, $Z=(1+e)(\zeta+V)-\zeta$ takes $J_{(\eta,\zeta)}$ to $(H_i')$, since each generator acquires the unit factor $(1+e)^{d_i}$. Hence $H_{K'}\le H_{J_{(\eta,\zeta)}}\le H_J=H_K$. The pure-$V$ degree-$d_i$ part is $H_i(0,V)\ne0$ by step 5, so $\operatorname{ord}f_i'\le d_i$.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case I, (7.28)--(7.29).

proof.text:
Suppose all $f_i'$ in this chart have order $d_i$. For a block whose generators retain order, differentiation gives
$$\partial_V^{\beta_j}f'_{i(j)}=e^{-1}\sigma^*g_j=:g_j',\qquad \partial_{V_k}g_j'=\sigma^*(\partial_{Z_k}g_j).$$
Their constant terms are the corresponding rows of the original invertible block Jacobian applied to $\zeta^\ell$. Their vanishing forces $\zeta^\ell=0$. In particular $\zeta=0$, so the point is on the strict transform of $N$. Restricting $f_i'$ to all complementary variables zero gives precisely $H_i(0,V)$: its terms of degree below $d_i$ vanish by the order assumption, and its degree-$d_i$ terms are the original pure-$Z$ ones. Step 5 supplies (2) for every prefix. The displayed derivative identities give (4), with the same Jacobian. For (5), $\partial_{V^\ell}^{\beta}f_i'=e^{|\beta|-d_i}\sigma^*(\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\beta}f_i)$ belongs to $(V^\ell)$ after inverting $e$. It is a regular series, and $(V^\ell)$ is $e$-saturated (its quotient is a power-series domain). Therefore it already belongs to $(V^\ell)$ before localization. This proves (1),(2),(4),(5) under retention of all orders.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case I, assertion (a), verification of (1),(2),(4),(5).

proof.text:
For (3), use the quotient estimate of [lem-trf-coordinate-blowup-division-generators]. If $f\in K$ has $P$-order $v$ and supported division $f=\sum q_if_i$, then
$$e^{-v}\sigma^*f=\sum_i(e^{d_i-v}\sigma^*q_i)f_i'.$$
All coefficients here are regular; they keep their prescribed supports because the vertices have zero $W$ components, $\zeta=0$, and the substitution scales $Z$ without translating it. The same holds after multiplication by $e^b$, $b\ge0$. Now let $g=\sum a_if_i'\in K'$, using the finite-generation clause of the same node. Approximate each $a_i$ by a polynomial $A_i$ of degree at most $k$, and set $h=\sum A_if_i'$. Then $g-h\in( X')^{k+1}$. Set $d=\max d_i$. Clearing the chart ratios in $e^{k+d}h$ gives the pullback of an $f\in K\cap P^{k+d}$: in the $i$th coefficient each degree-$t$ monomial of $A_i$ contributes a denominator of degree at most $t\le k$, and multiplication by $e^{k+d-d_i}$ clears it with nonnegative remaining exponent. If $v=\operatorname{ord}_P f$, then $v\ge k+d$ and $h=e^{v-k-d}(e^{-v}\sigma^*f)$. Thus every $h$ is a supported sum. By the closed-image clause of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division], the limit $g$ is also a supported sum. This proves (3). Its Hilbert criterion gives $H_{K'}=H_D=H_K$.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case I, assertion (a), verification of (3), cases (i)--(iii).

proof.text: If an order drops, take the first degree block $d_0$ with such a generator. Earlier blocks retain their orders, so the argument of step 8 applies to their accumulated essential variables: $\zeta^\ell=0$, homogeneous division holds for that prefix, and (5) makes every coefficient of a later $f_i'$ whose transverse exponent is in that prefix diagram and whose total degree is below $d_0$ vanish identically. Choose a nonzero least homogeneous component $F$ of a dropping generator; its degree $m<d_0$ and its support is outside the prefix diagram. Hence $F$ is a nonzero remainder and is independent of the supported prefix division columns in degree $m$. Those columns already number exactly $\#\{\alpha\in D:|\alpha|=m\}$, since later vertices have degree at least $d_0$. Through degree $m$, the earlier supported division columns are independent, number exactly $\#\{\alpha\in D:|\alpha|\le m\}$, and their span has zero intersection with nonzero remainders: apply uniqueness and the order estimate of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] to the retained prefix family $f_i'$, whose initial forms have homogeneous division by step 8; a supported prefix sum congruent modulo $(X')^{m+1}$ to a series supported outside the prefix diagram has that series in $(X')^{m+1}$. The degree-$m$ series $F$ is an additional independent relation modulo $(X')^{m+1}$, so $H_{K'}(m)<H_D(m)$. Step 7 gives the non-strict inequality in every degree. Thus $H_{K'}<H_K$. For the first block the prefix diagram is empty and this is simply the existence of a new relation of degree below the first vertex. Together with step 9 this proves equality if and only if all generator orders are retained in these charts.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case I, assertion (b), using (2) and (5) for the last retained block.

proof.text:
If every $\eta_j=0$, choose $\zeta_1=1$. The other chart is
$$T=S,\quad Y=eU,\quad Z_1=e,\quad Z_j=e(\zeta_j+V_j)\ (j>1).$$
The restrictions of $f_i'$ at $S=e=0$ are the dehomogenized $H_i(U,1,\widetilde\zeta+\widetilde V)$. As in step 7, step 4 bounds $H_{K'}$ by the Hilbert function of this homogeneous-transform ideal. The invertible substitution $T=S$, $Y=(1+e)U$, $Z_1=e$, $Z_j=(1+e)(\zeta_j+V_j)-\zeta_j$ identifies it, up to factors $(1+e)^{d_i}$, with $J_{(0,\zeta)}$. Step 6 makes its Hilbert function strictly below $H_J=H_K$. Thus these directions never give equality. In the $Y$ charts, step 8 excludes $\zeta\ne0$ at equality, so all equality points lie on the strict transform of $N$.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 7.20, Case II, (7.30).

proof.text:
At a point of $N'$ write its transverse coordinates as $Z'=Z/e$. Direct substitution, with $\zeta=0$, gives
$$f_i'=\sum_\gamma c'_{i\gamma}(W')(Z')^\gamma,\qquad c'_{i\gamma}=e^{|\gamma|-d_i}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}.$$
For $|\gamma|<d_i$ regularity follows from $c_{i\gamma}\in I_{C\subset N}^{d_i-|\gamma|}$ proved in step 3; for higher $|\gamma|$ the expression involves multiplication by a nonnegative power of $e$. Coefficientwise, $\operatorname{ord}f_i'\ge d_i$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{ord}c'_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$; the higher terms impose no condition. The upper bound in step 7 makes this equivalent to equality of each generator order. Steps 8--11 now give exactly the asserted equality criterion, the persistence of all five conditions and the same diagram. Regular membership and division here are on the coefficient space $N'$, where the center ideal pulls back to $(e)$, as required for the stated regular coefficient quotients.

source.place: BM Theorem 7.20(2)--(3), formula (7.19), and proof of Theorem 9.4, printed p.278.

proof.text: For a boundary intersection transverse to $N$, use $C=V(W_1,W_2)$ and the chart $W_1=W'_1$, $W_2=W'_1(c+W'_2)$, other $W$ unchanged, $Z=Z'$. Set $f_i'=\sigma^*f_i$ and $K'=(f_i')$. Substitution does not lower ordinary order; moreover $\operatorname{in}f_i'(0,Z')=H_i(0,Z')\ne0$, so each order is $d_i$. The homogeneous restriction test (step 5), separately for every prefix, supplies (2). The $Z$ derivatives commute with this substitution; their ideal membership and their constant Jacobians therefore retain (4),(5). By [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division], $H_{K'}\le H_D=H_K$. Applying step 4 to $h_i=f_i$, $U=(W_1,W_2)$ and all other variables as $V$ gives the reverse inequality, so $H_{K'}=H_K$. The same division node now gives (3). The coefficient formula is ordinary pullback since $Z$ was unchanged. The other chart interchanges $W_1,W_2$. This is the total-transform operation stipulated in the statement, at corresponding closed points.

source.place: BM Lemma 7.26 and proof of Theorem 7.21, printed pp.270,273; proof of Theorem 9.4.

proof.text: Adjoin an independent variable $t$. Each supported expansion extends coefficientwise in $t$; the homogeneous bases and the Jacobian identities extend too. No coefficient is changed except by ordinary pullback. Monomials outside $D\times\mathbf N$ of total degree at most $n$ are counted by $\sum_{j=0}^n H_K(j)$, as also stated by [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control]. All displayed identities and division bases commute with coefficient-field extension: at each jet order they are finite-dimensional matrix identities, and invertible determinants stay invertible. At an exceptional point one first extends to its residue field to make its homogeneous direction rational. Apply the same jet node to an affine coordinate ring of $X$, at $b\in X$; its etale Taylor compatibility identifies these jet dimensions on etale coefficient charts. For regular coefficient models use $\tau_b,\tau_b^N$ of [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus], formed after base change to $L=\kappa(b)$ at its rational point. That statement identifies substituted coefficients with $\tau_b^N((\partial_y^\delta c)|_N)/\delta!$ and says these formulas commute with field extension. Its faithful-flatness clause contracts the resulting equalities of extended finite ideals to the regular stalks, then coherence gives equality germs. The use of the extended Taylor function at nonclosed points is essential; no identification with the uncorrected local Hilbert--Samuel function is made. In the Lean field-extension clause, use [lem-trf-formal-division-scalar-extension] for conditions (2),(3), and [lem-trf-formal-jet-length-scalar-extension] for each Hilbert value. For (1), coefficient injectivity preserves the least nonzero degree and ideal extension preserves membership. The coefficient formula for a partial derivative commutes with the field homomorphism, and induction along the derivative list proves the same for iterated derivatives. The image of each transverse variable generates the corresponding target ideal, so its derivative membership tests persist. Applying the field map to the Jacobian determinant preserves its unit property; the determinant permutation formula identifies it with the transformed Jacobian. These steps prove (4),(5) and assemble all five conditions without a new assumption.

source.place: BM proof of Theorem 9.4; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BMT 6.2. Agent explanation of the residue-field and etale conventions.

proof_origin.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the local literature route. Detailed reconstruction follows BM 7.3--7.7, 7.14, 7.20--7.26 and proof of 9.4, read online; BM is absent from literature, hence agent origin under the standing brief. V2 (2026-10-26) formalizes the field-extension clause of step 14 with two explicit scalar-extension intermediates and direct coefficient, order, derivative, ideal and determinant proofs; the other eight theorem plans remain open.
